evidence.paraphrase: The story's world features an all-encompassing government that controls every aspect of life.
evidence.quote:
The Government was ubiquitous,
omnipresent and omnipotent. It dominated every conversation, every
business, every life from birth to death.

evidence.paraphrase: In this society everyone except Brandon is employed by the government, and he alone runs a private business.
evidence.quote:
He's the only person not
employed by the government, the only one still operating a private
business!

evidence.paraphrase: Government employee salaries are automatically adjusted by computers to match government expenses, keeping the budget balanced.
evidence.quote:
Calculators and computers adjust our
salary each year in proportion to the expense of the government. We
have been operating out of the red that way for years.

evidence.paraphrase: Because Brandon is the sole remaining taxpayer, an entire government bureau exists only to process his forms and runs at a loss.
evidence.quote:
Brandon was the last taxpayer. We've
been forced to operate an entire bureau just to process his forms. It's
the only department operating in the red.

evidence.paraphrase: The growing complexity of tax forms consumes ever more of Brandon's year, portrayed as an inescapable trap.
evidence.quote:
One hundred days!" Evans laughed. "Soon it'll be every day of the
year. Then where will you be?" He looked directly into Brandon's eyes.
"Can't you see? You're in the web already, working a third of the year
without compensation.

evidence.paraphrase: The President reverses expected power relations, concluding that the lone remaining taxpayer is the government's true boss.
evidence.quote:
After all, the government
works for the taxpayers, Evans--and Brandon is the last taxpayer. He's
our boss, son. The only boss we have left.

evidence.paraphrase: The President reasons that if no taxpayers remained, the government would have no justification to exist.
evidence.quote:
If the sole
purpose of the government is to serve the taxpayers--and there were no
more--how could we justify our existence in office?

evidence.paraphrase: The government deliberately engineered worthless job offers and loaded tax forms as a calculated strategy to break Brandon's resistance.
evidence.quote:
They had
known Brandon was a stubborn man, that was why things were done as they
were. The offering of worthless positions had been a feint. He should
have grabbed at something he could handle. And the tax forms! That was
supposed to be the last straw. They had been loaded, prepared just for
Brandon, to break his resistence.

evidence.paraphrase: The Secretary, disturbed by his role, smashes one of Brandon's puppets on the ground.
evidence.quote:
Suddenly,
he slammed it to the ground. The paint chipped and cracked. The small
head rolled loosely across the lawn.

evidence.paraphrase: Brandon suddenly realizes why he has resisted giving up his puppet-making work.
evidence.quote:
For the first time it
was clear to him why he had been so reluctant to give up his work.

evidence.paraphrase: Government employees never file taxes; they receive a flat salary with subsistence provided.
evidence.quote:
Government employees never do. We are paid a flat sum and our
subsistance is taken care of.
